steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Hey, you're the one who invited me. Say something. I skipped the banquet celebrating the completion of the First Temple for you, you know.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You were a big part of getting the work across the finish line the day before the exchange ceremony. Tradition calls for a full day of celebration. The craftsmen began drinking and reciting poetry in broad daylight.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Not all of them hold their drink well. Guess the peace officers will have their hands full tonight.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Kantia from the moving crew, right? She's really taken to you after you helped her a few times.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yeah... it's been like a dream, coming to Athenius.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Right you are.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: First day in Athenius, you solved the dispute between the fruit farmers and craftsmen. Then you became the supervisor of the final phase of the temple rebuilding project.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: And you chased Xanthos over multiple blocks after the harp was stolen.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Way more interesting than just escorting a relic, isn't it?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: But my job was to ensure that the exchange ceremony goes smoothly, and promote the friendship between our two nations.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What's the matter, Titi? This isn't like you.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Pallas...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The harp of Kereseira we brought... it's a replica.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I would never have known, if the harp wasn't damaged during my scuffle with Xanthos.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Now, my deputy, Behnui, wants to fulfill the padishah's mission by handing over the fake harp in the exchange ceremony... but I know that's not right.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The ceremony is tomorrow. Do you have a solution?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: There's no good way to do this. We'd need a miracle.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I read through every relevant book I could borrow from the Bibliotheka of Athenius. I learned that the harp of Kereseira was lost to war a long time ago, and it hasn't been seen since.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It's likely that the Sargonian craftsmen who made this replica had only seen the blueprints, not the harp itself.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Could the true harp still be in Minos? Or...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Or it was destroyed by the fires of war long ago... I'm sorry.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: There's no need for you to apologize.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What do you plan to do, if the true harp is nowhere to be found?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I can't publicly announce in my capacity as Sargonian ambassador that we brought a fake harp. It's more likely to lead to conflict than to reveal the truth.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: A very reasonable concern.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: And so, I'll have to stop the ceremony in my personal capacity.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I'm getting rid of the fake harp before the ceremony can start.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: You can't go in.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Look, I know a special visitor's permit is required to visit and deliver supplies. I just forgot.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Can you accommodate me this once? My old classmate went in a couple of days ago, all of a sudden. His family asked me to bring him some stuff.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Alright, to tell you the truth, he's pretty sick.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: The Athenian jail has a doctor and basic medicine, but it's not as effective as the Rhodes Island stuff. He could have an attack while in custody, if he doesn't get proper treatment.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: Save your breath, it's no use.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Alright. I didn't want to do this...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Here's my pass. Hekádemos, Grammateús to the Astynomos.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: I am authorized to enter detention facilities, even bring in suspects for questioning. Open the door. This is an order. I will file the necessary paperwork later.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: You want to see the two thieves who came in a few days ago?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Lykeion is not a...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Never mind. Yes.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: You can't.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: What? Why not?!

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: You are authorized to see prisoners held at the jail, but the two you're looking for aren't here anymore.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Were they transferred?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: That is unusual. Has Kyría Athopoulou's Oripathy treatment system been implemented already?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Where were they transferred?

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: Don't bother, Hekádemos. I don't know who they are to you, but not even the Grammateús to the Astynomos is authorized to see inmates on death row.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Death row?!

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: Sorry, Kyría Athopoulou...

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Does Lydia... I mean, does the Astynomos really not have the time?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I heard that Xanthos and his apprentice were arrested for theft.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: They're my patients, and in a key stage of treatment, as the Rhodes Island clinic already reported.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Xanthos's Blood Originium-Crystal Density is particularly high, which could potentially lead to an acute attack of Oripathy. I would like to deliver medicine to them...

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: Look, I don't understand any of the medical jargon you're throwing around.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: We are all very grateful to you for returning to Athenius, bringing back medical knowledge that you learned abroad and establishing an Oripathy clinic, but...

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: I shouldn't talk too much, but you're a good doctor, and the Astynomos' sister. You really should keep your distance from her for a few days at least, if only for the sake of your relationship.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: The official line says the crime was theft, but the Sargonian ambassador came here a few days ago and said the thing that was stolen wasn't the ambassador's personal item, but an important relic for the exchange ceremony.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: He put a lot of pressure on Lydia. They're probably going to be publicly charged with treason, once the ceremony is over.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Treason?! But according to Minoan law—

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: Most of the issues the Astynomos faces cannot be solved through legal procedures.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: She wants a new, modern Minos, and she is willing to give everything for it. That's why we're willing to work for her.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: Perhaps you're not aware, but she gave up her family inheritance, even chasing her other family out of Athenius after taking office...

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: She gave up her inheritance?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I thought the business failed...

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: This exchange of relics is an important part of her administration. There must be no mistake, at least not on the surface... even if it means sacrificing two lives. It's not like they're innocent, after all.

steps.name: Clerk
steps.text: I'm sorry... I have to get back to work.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: What is Lydia...?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Well, she wouldn't meet with me, and I doubt I can convince her, even if we did meet.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: But Xanthos and Lykeion need to be tried fairly. I can't let Lydia make a mistake like this. What do I do?
Sorry, I was lost in thought—

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Kyría Athopoulou?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You've been staring out the window, Astynomos.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Apologies, Hiéreia Kassandra.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Why not let Kyría Athopoulou in? I have to discuss the establishment of an Oripathy treatment system with her anyway.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Oh? I thought you wanted to get extra help to plead the case of the two Infected who were arrested a few days ago.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You know that ferryman, Xanthos, quite well. I believe you were the one who found him the job at the crossing?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: The peace officers will deal with this theft. Neither of us need to worry about it.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I'm afraid I don't have that luxury. If this incident affects the trust between us and Sargon, then this incident will become more than a simple theft...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: It's my own business. It has nothing to do with a priestess of Endymion Temple.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Back on topic, Hiéreia Kassandra. The opening play for tomorrow's exchange ceremony has been decided. It is to be King Pertheus, a popular classic across Terra.

spans.text: Back on topic, Hiéreia Kassandra. The opening play for tomorrow's exchange ceremony has been decided. It is to be

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: All the priests need to do is attend. There will be no need for complicated rituals.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: A few weeks ago, I came to discuss the priest-directed ceremonial play for the completion of Kereseira's First Temple. I have not seen you at the Astynomos' Office since.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I apologize. My schedule is a busy one. I certainly remember. The exchange ceremony also requires an opening play, and we can kill two fowlbeasts with one stone this way. We need not bother the priests, however.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Excuse me, but the rebuilding of Kereseira's First Temple is a symbol of the people's spirit. Now that it is complete, tradition calls for a proper ceremony to invite the heroes to enter the temple and give Minos their blessings.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: The council is not trying to usurp your administrative power, and the exchange ceremony does fall within your responsibility.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: However, Minoan drama began as a ritualistic performance.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Every single detail is carefully arranged, from the props to the program to the performers. It's not enough to simply put on a popular play.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: 'Immortal legend'... 'witness of the oracle'... 'heroic relic'...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Do not think that I am completely ignorant of traditional ceremony, or that I'm one of those radicals who calls for every tradition to be abolished.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: But even if you have your choice of the program and control over the troupe, there is still something missing from the traditional ritual that you want, isn't there?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: ...The Sargonian mission brought Kereseira's harp.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Oh? You do recognize the relic's ritual significance?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: ...What do you mean?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I'm neither an archaeologist nor a historian. As Astynomos, however, I understand every priest who sits on the council, including you.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You are the head priestess of Endymion Temple, and endowed with the divine gift of speaking on behalf of the heroes. Your knowledge of heroic epics puts most scholars to shame.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Yet you showed no interest about the harp of Kereseira that the Sargonian mission brought with them. You didn't even ask to see it.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I don't know why exactly, but I can tell that the harp the Sargonian mission brought was not the heroic relic that you knew.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: The ceremonial play could not have been performed to begin with.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: No, I already...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I have nothing against the council, Hiéreia Kassandra. If you present a legitimate heroic relic for the ceremony, I would be more than happy to give the choice of play back to you.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: For the past century, however, the temples have mostly used crude replicas in place of true relics for your ceremonies. I don't need to tell you that the link between us and the heroes is weakening.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: As a modern state, Minos can no longer rely on ancient legends to unite our people's spirit. No need to worry, however. The temples and priests will continue to exist.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You can continue to contribute to historical research and tourism.
